scope: Actual side-view controls and downloads, original/daily assets, source timing, project reopen, all-frame alpha and registered head/hands protection, and fresh independent player after closing the workbench. Technical checks are not visual acceptance or proof that interpolated anchors are anatomically exact.
browserObservationScope: Canvas metadata is observed together with its drawing. Missed display ticks are reported, not treated as missing source frames. ZIP and GIF decoding checks every encoded frame independently.

idle.reason: Stable naturally standing recovery, same source identity as the selected run. Excludes the blink that turns directly into celebration.
limitations: Nearly static idle; no complete natural blink in this interval. Endpoint continuity still requires final matte/render review.

walk.reason: Complete right-and-left step cycle with relaxed arms, a low ranked boundary mismatch, and no omitted/interpolated source frames.
limitations: Brisk walk: full cycle is 0.75s. User previously found this source somewhat stiff; retain as candidate rather than claim visual acceptance. Source head/body shape differs slightly from 1885 after constant scaling.

run.reason: Complete two-step gait: passes support/recovery for both legs and both opposite arm swings; 18 consecutive original frames at24fps. f150 matches f132 phase well.
limitations: Original video shading and small hand/foot shape changes remain. No promise of physically correct world-displacement speed.

jump.reason: Original uninterrupted run-to-crouch approach, two consecutive jumps, and second landing compression. Preview as a two-hop action, not one jump.
limitations: Ends in shallow crouch. No neutral idle recovery or seamless repeated-jump loop is supplied.
Source blur, green spill and cross-source drawing differences remain.

walk.reason: Best existing female early-gait candidate with comparatively relaxed arms, both alternating support/pass phases, and matching start/end phase. This is a fast-walk candidate, not a fully accepted ordinary walk.
limitations: Some extended-foot poses appear briefly light or airborne; cannot certify continuous single-foot ground contact.

limitations: Generated shape/hand/foot fluctuations persist.
